findings.explanation: The SQL query is parameterized using SQLAlchemy's text function with a separate params argument, which mitigates the risk of SQL injection.

evidence.content: rows = session.execute(text("SELECT id, username, role FROM users WHERE " + where), params)
The text function in SQLAlchemy allows for parameterized SQL queries by separating the query string from the parameters, which helps prevent SQL injection.

evidence_issues: cited policy document does not exist: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/text.html#sql-expression-language-text

findings.explanation: The endpoint does not verify ownership of the user being filtered, allowing unauthorized access to other users' data.

evidence.content:
rows = session.execute(
    text("SELECT id, username, role FROM users WHERE " + where),
    params,
)

- A user may read or update ONLY their own profile (`/users/<id>`).
  Administrators may read or update any profile. Use
  `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id)` for this check.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a check to ensure the current user is either an admin or the owner of the user being filtered.
